title: Minimum Depth of Binary Tree
summary: Count the nodes on the shortest path from the root down to a leaf.

tests.explain: 5 is a leaf on level 2, so the shortest root-to-leaf path is 3 → 5: 2 nodes.
The root has only a right child, so it is not a leaf. The only leaf is 4, at depth 4.

hints: The minimum depth is the depth of the shallowest leaf. Which traversal meets shallow nodes first?
BFS visits the tree level by level, so the first leaf it dequeues is a shallowest leaf: return that level's depth right away.
A leaf has no left and no right child. A node with one child is not a leaf, so don't stop there. (With DFS, a missing child must not count as a depth-0 branch.)

complexity.time: O(n) in the worst case, but BFS stops at the first leaf and often visits far fewer nodes
complexity.space: O(w) for the queue, where w is the widest level it reaches
